newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK CABINET STARTS TALKS ON TOUGH BUDGET PLANS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK CABINET STARTS TALKS ON TOUGH BUDGET PLANS.

text.p: The Greek government started its full cabinet meeting on the 1997 budget which is expected to debate deep cuts in the spending at several ministries, official sources said.
Prime Minister Costas Simitis will preside over the cabinet meeting and will talk to reporters after it finishes, his office said.

National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou is due to hold a news conference after the meeting and give the first official indications of where cuts will be made and how he plans to raise Media reports, based on widespread leaks and speculation in recent days, have suggested deep cuts at some ministries and an array of possible new taxes.
The budget must be presented to parliament before the end of the month. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
